title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 2nd Truth Divine Speech

questions.question: What is identified as coming from the attribute of Speech at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Divine speech is presented as proceeding from the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the Qur’anic verse about the sea becoming ink suggest about Divine speech?
questions.answer: It suggests that Divine speech has no limit.

questions.question: What is described as the clearest sign that shows a being exists?
questions.answer: Speech is described as the clearest sign.

questions.question: Because speech shows existence, what does this truth testify to about Allah?
questions.answer: It testifies to His existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Which two strong proofs of this truth are named first?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What other source is mentioned as a wide proof besides revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: The sacred and heavenly books.

questions.question: Which source is described as the brightest and most inclusive proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the passage send readers to other sections instead of explaining everything here?
questions.answer: Because those sections already explain and establish this truth in detail.

questions.question: What was enough for the traveler at this point?
questions.answer: The lights and deeper meanings found in the noble verse were enough for him.

questions.question: What main truth does that verse support along with the earlier testimonies?
questions.answer: It supports the truth of Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: In the verse from Surah Al ‘Imran mentioned here, who besides Allah gives testimony?
questions.answer: The angels and people of knowledge.

questions.question: What quality is connected to that testimony in the same verse?
questions.answer: Justice and fairness are connected to it.

questions.question: In the statement from the Nineteenth Degree, how is Allah described in relation to existence?
questions.answer: He is described as the One whose existence is necessary.

questions.question: How is Allah described in relation to unity in that same statement?
questions.answer: He is described as One and absolutely unique.

questions.question: What belongs to Allah according to that summary statement?
questions.answer: His beautiful names, highest attributes, and the most exalted likeness belong to Him.

questions.question: What does the necessarily existent Essence point to?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s necessary existence together with His unity.

questions.question: Through what kind of agreement do Allah’s sacred attributes support this testimony?
questions.answer: They support it through their complete harmony and agreement.

questions.question: Through what kind of agreement do His beautiful names support it?
questions.answer: They support it through the harmony of their manifestations.

questions.question: Which broad reality is said to appear through the manifestation of dominicality?
questions.answer: The self-disclosure of divinity.

questions.question: Which actions are linked with will and power in the passage?
questions.answer: Bringing into being, creating, making, and originating.

questions.question: Which actions are linked with choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, arranging, and turning things in order.

questions.question: Which actions are linked with purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Spending out, protecting, organizing, governing, and providing sustenance.

questions.question: What do complete order and balance in these actions help testify to?
questions.answer: They help testify to Allah’s existence and oneness.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the role of the truths listed in the Nineteen Degrees of the First Chapter?
questions.answer: They show necessary existence through being present and also testify to divine unity through their broadness.

questions.question: Why were those truths treated first as proofs of Necessary Existence?
questions.answer: Because they show existence more openly and directly.

questions.question: In the Second Chapter, how will the same truths be treated differently?
questions.answer: They will be presented mainly as proofs of divine unity.

questions.question: What is the relationship between unity and necessity according to the passage?
questions.answer: Each one supports and proves the other.

questions.question: What wording was used repeatedly in the First Chapter to highlight its focus?
questions.answer: It used wording that pointed to the testimony of the greatness and comprehensiveness of a truth.

questions.question: What different wording will be used in the Second Chapter, and what does it emphasize?
questions.answer: It will use wording about witnessing that greatness and comprehensiveness, emphasizing the clear visibility of divine unity.

questions.question: Why does the writer say the explanation of the Second Chapter will be brief?
questions.answer: Because different obstacles forced him to keep it short.

questions.question: Where does the writer leave the fuller explanation of these matters?
questions.answer: He leaves it to other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What subject is introduced under “The Second Truth”?
questions.answer: The subject is Divine speech coming from the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What idea about Allah’s words is drawn from the verse about the sea becoming ink?
questions.answer: Allah’s words are beyond all limit.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat speech as so important in proving existence?
questions.answer: Because speech is presented as the most obvious sign that a speaker truly exists.

questions.question: What two beliefs are supported by the truth of Divine speech?
questions.answer: Allah’s existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Name the first pair of evidences given for this truth.
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What category of writings is offered as another proof?
questions.answer: Sacred and heavenly scriptures.

questions.question: Among the proofs listed, which one has the highest rank in brightness and scope?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage choose to do instead of repeating long explanations from earlier sections?
questions.answer: It briefly points readers back to those earlier discussions.

questions.question: Why is the cited verse enough for both the readers and the traveler?
questions.answer: Because it contains guiding light and deep meanings that confirm the truth.

questions.question: What verse is then quoted to summarize the lesson of this station?
questions.answer: The verse that says Allah testifies, and so do the angels and people of knowledge, that none is worthy of worship but Him.

questions.question: Which groups are presented as joining in testimony with Allah in that verse?
questions.answer: Angels and people who have knowledge.

questions.question: What moral quality appears in that verse alongside the testimony?
questions.answer: Upright justice.

questions.question: In the declaration from the Nineteenth Degree, what title is given to Allah regarding His existence?
questions.answer: He is the Necessarily Existent.

questions.question: What two words in that declaration stress Allah’s absolute oneness?
questions.answer: He is described as One and Unique.

questions.question: What three things are specially said to belong to Allah?
questions.answer: The beautiful names, the highest attributes, and the loftiest similitude.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in His unity according to the declaration?
questions.answer: The necessarily existent Essence itself points to it.

questions.question: How do Allah’s sacred and all-encompassing attributes relate to that proof?
questions.answer: Their united agreement confirms it.

questions.question: How do Allah’s beautiful names relate to that proof?
questions.answer: Their manifest agreement also confirms it.

questions.question: How do Allah’s qualities and acts contribute to this testimony?
questions.answer: Their active and harmonious operation supports the same truth.

questions.question: What reality is said to appear in the showing forth of dominicality?
questions.answer: The majesty of divinity becoming known.

questions.question: Which actions in the passage show activity tied to will and power?
questions.answer: Creating, bringing forth, crafting, and originating.

questions.question: Which actions show activity tied to choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, arranging, and revolving affairs.

questions.question: Which actions show activity tied to purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Directing, organizing, preserving, managing, and sustaining.

questions.question: What feature of these acts shows that they are not random?
questions.answer: They are carried out with full order and balance.

questions.question: Besides proving existence, what else did the truths of the Nineteen Degrees also prove?
questions.answer: They also proved Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: Why were those truths first counted mainly as proofs of Necessary Existence?
questions.answer: Because their clearest and most direct side was showing existence.

questions.question: In the Second Chapter, what side of those truths will be stressed?
questions.answer: Their clear proof of divine unity.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the connection between necessity and unity?
questions.answer: It says one of them proves the other.

questions.question: What shift in wording marks the change from the First Chapter to the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: The wording moves from testimony language to witnessing language.

questions.question: What is the purpose of this wording change?
questions.answer: It shows that in the Second Chapter the visible clarity of unity is being emphasized.

questions.question: Why will the discussion of the Second Chapter not be expanded here?
questions.answer: Because obstacles prevented a longer treatment.

questions.question: How does the writer handle that limitation?
questions.answer: He gives only a summary and leaves fuller explanation to other works in the collection.

questions.question: What divine attribute is directly connected to discourse in the passage?
questions.answer: The attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the verse about the ocean and ink teach about the scale of Allah’s speech?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s speech is limitless.

questions.question: In the passage, what is the strongest outward sign that someone exists?
questions.answer: Speaking is the strongest outward sign mentioned.

questions.question: If speech is a clear sign of existence, what does Divine speech prove about Allah?
questions.answer: It proves that Allah exists and that He is one.

questions.question: Which two means of divine communication are named as major evidences for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What written sources are also said to support this truth?
questions.answer: Holy and heavenly books.

questions.question: Which single source is described as especially brilliant and wide-ranging?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the passage avoid a full discussion of these evidences here?
questions.answer: Because that explanation has already been given elsewhere.

questions.question: What satisfied the traveler who could not continue farther?
questions.answer: The insight and illumination found in the verse were enough for him.

questions.question: What central belief is reinforced by the verse about Allah’s testimony, the angels, and the people of knowledge?
questions.answer: The belief that only Allah is truly divine.

questions.question: What does the inclusion of angels and knowledgeable people suggest about this testimony?
questions.answer: It suggests that this truth is confirmed by both heavenly beings and informed human witnesses.

questions.question: What standard is tied to Allah’s testimony in the verse?
questions.answer: Perfect justice.

questions.question: What does the phrase about necessary existence tell us about Allah?
questions.answer: His existence is not dependent or optional; it is absolutely necessary.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by pairing Allah’s names with His attributes?
questions.answer: It teaches that His names and attributes together point to who He is and confirm His perfection.

questions.question: What does the “most sublime similitude” suggest in this passage?
questions.answer: It suggests that the highest and most fitting description belongs to Allah alone.

questions.question: What gives witness to Allah’s necessary existence in unity according to the declaration?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent Essence, together with the agreement of His attributes and names, gives witness.

questions.question: How do the divine names function in this proof?
questions.answer: Their manifestations work together in agreement to confirm the truth.

questions.question: How do the divine acts function in this proof?
questions.answer: Their ordered and purposeful operation supports the same conclusion.

questions.question: What larger truth is shown in the unfolding of dominicality?
questions.answer: The reality of divinity showing itself.

questions.question: What do acts like creating and originating show about the way Allah acts?
questions.answer: They show action based on will and power.

questions.question: What do acts like shaping and regulating show about the way Allah acts?
questions.answer: They show action based on choice and wisdom.

questions.question: What do acts like preserving and nourishing show about the way Allah acts?
questions.answer: They show action based on purpose and mercy.

questions.question: Why are order and balance important in the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: They show that these actions come from perfect control, not confusion or chance.

questions.question: What double role did the nineteen truths of the First Chapter play?
questions.answer: They served as proofs of necessary existence and also as witnesses to unity.

questions.question: Which side of that double role was more obvious in the First Chapter?
questions.answer: Their proof of necessary existence was more obvious.

questions.question: Which side becomes the main focus in the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: Their proof of divine unity.

questions.question: Does the passage separate necessity and unity as unrelated ideas?
questions.answer: No. It says each one confirms the other.

questions.question: What does the movement from “testimony” to “witnessing” imply?
questions.answer: It implies a shift toward stressing how clearly unity can be seen.

questions.question: What reason is given for not explaining the later degrees in full detail?
questions.answer: Various obstacles prevented a full explanation.

questions.question: What attitude does the writer take because of those obstacles?
questions.answer: He keeps the discussion brief and concise.

questions.question: Where should a student look for fuller treatment of these ideas according to the passage?
questions.answer: In other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: At the beginning of the marked passage, what truth is linked to the attribute of Speech?
questions.answer: Divine communication is linked to it.

questions.question: How does the verse about the sea and ink help the reader understand Divine communication?
questions.answer: It shows that it cannot be exhausted or fully counted.

questions.question: What humanly understandable sign is used to show that a speaker exists?
questions.answer: The sign is speech.

questions.question: From that point, what conclusion does the passage draw about the Pre-Eternal Speaker?
questions.answer: It concludes that His existence and His unity are firmly testified to.

questions.question: What are the first two evidences named for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What additional kind of proof comes from transmitted writings?
questions.answer: Proof from holy and heavenly books.

questions.question: What makes the Qur’an stand out among the proofs mentioned?
questions.answer: It is described as the most radiant and most comprehensive proof.

questions.question: Why are readers directed to other degrees of the treatise?
questions.answer: Because those places already explain and confirm this matter.

questions.question: What was enough for the traveler who could go no farther?
questions.answer: The guidance and hidden meanings in the cited verse were enough.

questions.question: What does the passage say that verse adds to the earlier evidences?
questions.answer: It adds its own witness to them.

questions.question: In the next Qur’anic verse quoted, who bears witness along with Allah?
questions.answer: The angels and the people of knowledge.

questions.question: What does the phrase connected to fairness show about Allah’s testimony?
questions.answer: It shows that His testimony is established with perfect justice.

questions.question: How is Allah introduced in the summary statement that follows?
questions.answer: As the one true God whose existence is necessary and who is absolutely one.

questions.question: What does the passage say belongs to Allah in terms of names and attributes?
questions.answer: The most beautiful names and the highest attributes belong to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the highest likeness or supreme example?
questions.answer: It belongs to Allah as well.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in that statement?
questions.answer: The necessarily existent Essence points to it.

questions.question: What role do the sacred attributes play in that proof?
questions.answer: Their combined agreement supports and confirms it.

questions.question: What role do the beautiful names play in that proof?
questions.answer: Their manifested agreement also confirms it.

questions.question: What role do the divine acts and qualities play in that proof?
questions.answer: Their active and united testimony strengthens it.

questions.question: Which great truth is said to appear through the display of dominicality?
questions.answer: The truth of divinity revealing itself.

questions.question: Which set of actions is connected with will and power?
questions.answer: Bringing into existence, creating, crafting, and originating.

questions.question: Which set of actions is connected with choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, managing, and circulating affairs.

questions.question: Which set of actions is connected with purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Directing, arranging, preserving, governing, and feeding.

questions.question: What overall pattern in these acts points away from randomness?
questions.answer: Their complete order and balance.

questions.question: What did the truths in the Nineteen Degrees indicate through their very existence and presence?
questions.answer: They indicated Necessary Existence.

questions.question: What did those same truths show through their breadth and all-including nature?
questions.answer: They showed Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: Why were they first treated under the heading of Necessary Existence?
questions.answer: Because that was the clearest and most explicit part of their proof.

questions.question: How will they be treated in the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: As proofs of divine unity in a more direct way.

questions.question: According to the passage, how are unity and necessity related?
questions.answer: They are mutually supporting, with each proving the other.

questions.question: What verbal distinction is used between the two chapters?
questions.answer: The first uses language of testimony, while the second uses language of witnessing.

questions.question: What does this distinction help the reader notice?
questions.answer: It helps the reader notice the clear visibility of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Why is the explanation here short rather than detailed?
questions.answer: Because the writer faced obstacles and had to be brief.

questions.question: What source is expected to provide the fuller explanation later?
questions.answer: Other sections of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What topic opens the marked section?
questions.answer: The topic is Divine discourse arising from the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the verse about the sea becoming ink imply about the amount of Divine speech?
questions.answer: It implies that Divine speech is endless.

questions.question: What evidence does the passage call the clearest sign that a being exists?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: Since that sign is present in the divine sense, what does it become a testimony for?
questions.answer: It becomes a testimony for Allah’s existence and unity.

questions.question: What two evidences are mentioned first and said to be discussed elsewhere?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What broad proof is mentioned after those two?
questions.answer: The sacred and heavenly books.

questions.question: Which proof is described with the strongest praise in the list?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the writer choose instead of repeating the full proofs in this section?
questions.answer: He refers readers to the other degrees where those proofs are explained.

questions.question: What was sufficient for the traveler at this stopping point?
questions.answer: The insight and mysteries contained in the noble verse were sufficient.

questions.question: What does the verse about Allah, the angels, and those with knowledge mainly affirm?
questions.answer: It affirms that there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does the presence of learned people in that verse show about the testimony?
questions.answer: It shows that sound knowledge agrees with this truth.

questions.question: What does the verse connect with Allah’s testimony besides oneness?
questions.answer: It connects it with steadfast justice.

questions.question: How is Allah described at the start of the statement from the Nineteenth Degree?
questions.answer: As the one true God who necessarily exists, and who is one and unique.

questions.question: What three honors are said to belong to Allah there?
questions.answer: Beautiful names, supreme attributes, and the highest similitude.

questions.question: What directly points to Allah’s necessary existence in unity?
questions.answer: The necessarily existent Essence.

questions.question: How do Allah’s sacred attributes support this pointing?
questions.answer: All of them agree together in confirming it.

questions.question: How do His beautiful names support it?
questions.answer: Their manifestations also agree together in confirming it.

questions.question: How do His actions and qualities support it?
questions.answer: Their active operation gives further testimony.

questions.question: What truth is described as appearing through the manifestation of dominicality?
questions.answer: The truth of divinity making itself known.

questions.question: Which actions reveal divine activity in connection with will and power?
questions.answer: Creating, bringing into being, making, and originating.

questions.question: Which actions reveal divine activity in connection with choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Determining, shaping, regulating, and ordering movement.

questions.question: Which actions reveal divine activity in connection with purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Disposing, preserving, organizing, managing, and sustaining.

questions.question: What two qualities describe the way all these actions are carried out?
questions.answer: They are carried out with perfect order and balance.

questions.question: In the note, what did the truths from the Nineteen Degrees prove most openly?
questions.answer: They proved Necessary Existence most openly.

questions.question: What else did those truths also attest because of their comprehensiveness?
questions.answer: They also attested Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: How will the truths be designated in the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: They will be designated as proofs of divine unity.

questions.question: In that new designation, how is necessity related to unity?
questions.answer: Necessity is still present, but more indirectly, while unity is shown directly.

questions.question: What principle does the passage give about unity and necessity?
questions.answer: Unity proves necessity, and necessity proves unity.

questions.question: What repeated phrase marked the First Chapter’s style?
questions.answer: A phrase stressing testimony to the greatness and comprehensiveness of the truth.

questions.question: What repeated phrase will mark the Second Chapter’s style?
questions.answer: A phrase stressing the witnessing of that greatness and comprehensiveness.

questions.question: What idea is highlighted by the new phrase in the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: The plainly observable character of divine unity.

questions.question: Why did the writer not explain the degrees of the Second Chapter in the same way as the First?
questions.answer: Obstacles prevented him from doing so.

questions.question: What final step does the writer take because of that limitation?
questions.answer: He leaves the full explanation to other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What aspect of Allah is the “Second Truth” about?
questions.answer: It is about Divine speech connected to the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: How does the passage interpret the Qur’anic image of an ocean turned into ink?
questions.answer: It interprets it as showing the endlessness of Allah’s words.

questions.question: What sign is called the most obvious proof that a being is real?
questions.answer: Speech is called that proof.

questions.question: What does this make Divine discourse an endless witness to?
questions.answer: To Allah’s existence and His unity.

questions.question: Which two channels of divine communication are named as strong evidences?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What class of texts is named as another broad evidence?
questions.answer: Sacred and heavenly books.

questions.question: Which book is said to be the brightest and most comprehensive proof of all?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why are readers referred to other degrees in the treatise?
questions.answer: Because those degrees contain the detailed explanation and confirmation of this truth.

questions.question: What was enough for the traveler who stopped at this point?
questions.answer: The lights and subtle meanings found in the exalted verse were enough.

questions.question: What does that verse do in relation to the earlier testimonies?
questions.answer: It joins them and adds its own confirmation.

questions.question: In the next quoted verse, who are mentioned as sharing in testimony besides Allah?
questions.answer: The angels and those who possess knowledge.

questions.question: What does the mention of those with knowledge imply about faith and understanding?
questions.answer: It implies that true knowledge supports the belief in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What quality of Allah’s rule is highlighted in that verse?
questions.answer: Its perfect justice.

questions.question: What names for Allah in the summary statement emphasize that He has no partner?
questions.answer: The titles One and Unique emphasize that.

questions.question: What part of the statement emphasizes that Allah does not depend on anything else for His being?
questions.answer: The description of Him as necessarily existent.

questions.question: What possessions of Allah are named to show His perfection?
questions.answer: His beautiful names, supreme attributes, and the highest similitude.

questions.question: What is the basic source of the proof for Allah’s necessary existence in unity?
questions.answer: The necessarily existent Essence itself.

questions.question: How do the divine attributes contribute to that proof?
questions.answer: Their complete agreement confirms it.

questions.question: How do the divine names contribute to that proof?
questions.answer: Their manifestations agree in confirming it as well.

questions.question: How do divine deeds contribute to that proof?
questions.answer: Their active and ordered operation bears witness to it.

questions.question: What truth is displayed in the appearing of dominicality?
questions.answer: The truth of divinity displaying itself.

questions.question: What cluster of actions shows operation through will and power?
questions.answer: Bringing forth, creating, making, and originating.

questions.question: What cluster of actions shows operation through choice and wisdom?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, arranging, and directing cycles.

questions.question: What cluster of actions shows operation through purpose and mercy?
questions.answer: Directing affairs, organizing, preserving, governing, and providing livelihood.

questions.question: What general characteristics unify all these acts?
questions.answer: They are marked by complete order and balance.

questions.question: What two kinds of proof were found in the nineteen truths of the First Chapter?
questions.answer: Proof of Necessary Existence and proof of divine unity.

questions.question: Why were those truths mainly treated as proofs of Necessary Existence in the First Chapter?
questions.answer: Because they showed existence in the clearest and most explicit way.

questions.question: What will be the main role of those truths in the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: They will mainly serve as proofs of divine unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the link between these two doctrines?
questions.answer: Each one proves and strengthens the other.

questions.question: How does the repeated wording change from the First Chapter to the Second Chapter?
questions.answer: The wording changes from “by the testimony” to “by the witnessing.”

questions.question: What is the purpose of making that wording change?
questions.answer: To point out the visible and evident nature of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: Why is the treatment of the Second Chapter concise?
questions.answer: Because various obstacles made a detailed treatment impossible.

questions.question: According to the last sentence, where should the fuller explanation be sought?
questions.answer: In other portions of the Risale-i Nur.
